title: Camera shots
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers representation through lighting, framing and editing rather than the shot sizes (long, mid and close-up) and what each shot guides the viewer to notice, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Camera shots
card: shows a whole character and a wide view of the setting. It tells the viewer where the scene is set and how big or empty the place is.
frames a character from about the waist up. It shows body language, such as posture, gestures and how people stand near each other.
fills the frame with a face or a small object. It draws the viewer to an emotion, such as fear, or to a telling detail, such as a shaking hand.
A filmmaker chooses each shot to guide what the viewer notices. The same scene can feel quite different when it is filmed in a different shot.
draft.remember: Long shots show the place, mid shots show body language, close-ups show emotion or detail.

a.q: A film shows a girl alone on a vast, empty salt plain, so small she is almost a speck. Which shot is this?
opts: A long shot, which shows the setting
A mid shot, which shows body language
A mid shot, which shows the setting
a.why: The wide view of the salt plain and the tiny figure make this a long shot, which shows the setting. A mid shot frames a character from the waist up, so it could not show the whole plain.
a.clue: Think about how much of the place the viewer can see.

b.q: In a scene, Tomas waits outside a principal's office. The camera fills the frame with his hand, tapping his knee faster and faster. What does this shot most likely guide the viewer to notice?
opts: A telling detail that hints at his nerves
The layout of the school corridor
How he stands next to the other students
His whole body and where he is sitting
b.why: A shot filled by one hand is a close-up, which draws the viewer to a small detail. Here the tapping hints at nerves. A mid shot would show posture and gestures, and a long shot would show the corridor.
b.clue: How much of the frame does the hand fill?

a.best: A long shot, which shows the setting

b.best: A telling detail that hints at his nerves
